tytul: Pickled radish seed pods for the refrigerator
wstep: This card follows the Redemption Permaculture recipe for pickled radish seed pods, checked against the Oregon State University Extension rules for quick pickles; JarAtlas keeps them up to 2 weeks in the refrigerator.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Oregon State University Extension advises that quick pickles have at least as much vinegar as water, with vinegar of 5% acidity; this recipe uses equal parts, so do not add more water or less vinegar.
Use only vinegar labelled 5% acidity; white and cider vinegar can be used interchangeably; do not use wine vinegars, homemade vinegar or lemon juice.

The source says the pods keep up to a month in the refrigerator, but this is not a tested recipe: University of Wisconsin Extension says untested recipes can be prepared and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, and not on the counter.

These pickles are not heat processed, so they must be kept refrigerated; do not decrease the amount of vinegar, because an unsafe product may result; for a milder taste add sugar rather than reduce the vinegar.

akapity: 1 cup of radish seed pods, 1/2 cup of white vinegar and 1/2 cup of water.
The recipe uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.
The brine also has 1 tablespoon of salt, 1 tablespoon of sugar, a garlic clove and a bay leaf.
Vinegar with less than 5% acidity should never be used in home food preservation.
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, vegetables and water in the recipe.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): do not replace it with a stronger vinegar and do not dilute a stronger vinegar with water yourself; Penn State Extension advises staying within 5–7% acidity for home food preservation and diluting vinegar only when a tested recipe says so.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): use sterilized jars, as an Ask Extension expert advises for refrigerator pickles, and sterilize them as UGA directs for flavored vinegars: wash them in warm, soapy water, then immerse them completely in boiling water for 10 minutes.
Bring the brine to a boil, add the pods and simmer them, covered, for about 10 minutes.
Transfer them to the jar, making sure the pods are covered with brine.
Let the jar cool, then refrigerate it straight away.
The pods are ready after 24 hours.
Use them within 2 weeks and do not store them on the counter.
These pickles are not heat processed, so they are not shelf-stable at room temperature and must be kept in the refrigerator.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the jar on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door: Wisconsin Extension assumes 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder for refrigerator pickles, while a Polish sanitary inspection office gives about 10 °C for the door, even though it suggests the door for jars of preserves.
Fresh vegetables, except most tomatoes, are low-acid foods, with a pH above 4.6.
The acid level must be adequate and even throughout the product to prevent the growth of botulism bacteria.
